title: RWB-S6-E6012-APP: the cap slice has no plan row for the five consumed contracts, no cap parameter row, no cap route rule, no published trigger, no headroom column and no service contract baseline
source: Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings, R5.4, R5.5, R5.6, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S6-E6012-APP (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, C, I and X empty; patterns DP03 and DP19); context pack S6 rwb-debtsale (service row, 2 tables, 5 REST operations, 1 event, 0 jobs, 1 workflow, Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 5, 8 and 13, Temporal and Drools slides 5, 12 and 13); legacy RWB-E6-012 (Epic E6, release 30 April 2027, FEAT-DBS-16, depends on FEAT-DBS-01, AC1 and AC2, TC-E6-012-01 to TC-E6-012-04); FSD S6 Debt sale v3 A1.2, A2.1, A2.16, A2.16.3.1, A2.16.3.3, A2.16.4.1, A2.16.4.4, Requirements served and Screens; TSD S6 Debt sale v2 T2, T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T3.3, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1, T-A.1 and T-A.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-19 and R-DS-23; Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-DBS-16; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 row BR-050
section: Metadata (Dependencies and Patterns applied); Sections 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.3, 12.4, 12.6, 12.7, 12.8, 13, 14, 17, 18 and 19
description: (1) Consumed contracts have no plan row: the plan gives H = RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON with C, I and X empty, while the step reads the rwb-case cap row and reference data, the rwb-case case list, the rwb-source-data exposure, the rwb-decision package and the rwb-access capability area, so five consumed rows are C dependencies in fact and in no metadata row. (2) The rule kit is absent: DP-04 is not in the pattern set of this key although the step evaluates the Debt sale package, so RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON are absent. (3) The parameter and reference-data rows are absent: DP-06 and DP-07 are not in the pattern set although the cap and the four lists are the rows of E1-042 and E1-043, whose default owner is P3 rwb-case. (4) The access guard is absent: DP-08 is not in the pattern set although TSD S6 T6.1 declares a capability area and a right per surface and the legacy permission table gives the Case record right R to a long role list. (5) The event library is absent: DP-09 is not in the pattern set although the service owns topic rwb.debtsale.events.v1 and the schema carries outbox_event. (6) The scheduler pattern is absent: DP-10 is not in the pattern set although the legacy story says the work runs as a service or a scheduled job, the context pack lists 0 jobs for S6 and FSD S6 A2.16.2 step 1 names a timer as one possible trigger. (7) The cap row is unnamed: no source publishes the field, the row key, the version or the basis of the policy cap, and the only published figure is the wording the 54 percent cap of R-DS-19, R-DS-23 and FSD S6 A2.1, so the parameter read and its message are placeholders. (8) The cap has no route rule: FSD S6 A2.16.3.1 lists only VR-S6-016-1 and BR-S6-016, and the only rows naming the cap are R-DS-19 and R-DS-23 at the award, which are also the rows of RWB-S6-E6005-APP. (9) The trigger is unpublished and contradictory: A2.16.2 step 1 says a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer while A2.16.4.4 says No background event, so the step has no event, no job, no Schedule and no frequency. (10) The headroom has no column: no field of debt_sale_lot or debt_sale_account in TSD S6 T3.1 carries a cap position or a headroom, the legacy Data table names only decision_log_entry and rule_row, and DP-15 is not in the pattern set, so the figure is recorded in the decision record only. (11) No operation carries the element: TSD S6 T-A publishes five operations and none is a cap or headroom operation, the legacy Endpoints row says None, and the element is embedded in the lot read API-S6-002 of sibling stories. (12) The slice has no service contract baseline: a CON story for this legacy key is not in the plan, so the element shape, the consumed rows, the error set and the fakes have no owned baseline. (13) The plan carries no requirement id although FSD S6 requirements served gives REQ-S6-001 and the epic BRD gives BR-050. (14) No message is published for an absent cap row, so X3 records its reason without a message id.
evidence: Split plan H row of RWB-S6-E6012-APP = RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON with C, I, X empty and patterns DP03 and DP19; context pack S6 rows: tables debt_sale_lot and debt_sale_account, REST operations API-S6-001 to API-S6-005, event EV-23, jobs 0, workflow DebtSaleWorkflow; FSD S6 A2.16.2 step 1 and A2.16.4.4; FSD S6 A2.16.3.1 rows VR-S6-016-1 and BR-S6-016 with no route rule, and A2.16.3.3 roles None, runs unattended and Debt sale officer; TSD S6 T3.1 field list DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-037 with no cap or headroom column; TSD S6 T-A.1 five operations, none a cap operation; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-19 and R-DS-23, the only rows naming the 54 percent cap; legacy RWB-E6-012 Endpoints row None and Data rows decision_log_entry and rule_row; Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings (parameters E1-042 and reference data E1-043 with P3 rwb-case)
area: Contract, dependency, parameter, rule, trigger, data model and traceability
legacy_ref: RWB-E6-012; FEAT-DBS-16; R-DS-19; R-DS-23; BR-050; REQ-S6-001
owner_role: Solution architect with the owners of rwb-case (P3), rwb-decision (P7), rwb-access (P4) and rwb-source-data (P1), and the business owner of the debt sale cap
proposed: Publish the five consumed operations with their fake; add C rows for rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-access and rwb-source-data; add the DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-08 and DP-09 rows the tables need; name the cap row, its version, its basis and its owner; publish one route rule for the cap or confirm that R-DS-19 and R-DS-23 are its only test and which story owns them; publish the trigger or confirm the call from the lot build and award steps; add the cap-position and headroom fields or confirm the decision record as their only home; create the service contract baseline for this legacy key; and carry REQ-S6-001 and BR-050 in the plan
